assumptions: 'Success rate' means attempt-level success rate: successful attempts divided by all attempts, with each retry counted as a separate attempt. Order-level and technical rates are shown alongside.

The period analysed is 17 Sep 2026, compared against the immediately preceding period of equal length (16 Sep 2026). The detailed comparisons above use the anomaly window of 17-18 Sep against the baseline of 10-16 Sep.

facts.text: Across 17-18 Sep the attempt success rate fell 3.10pp from 90.07% (83,268 attempts in the baseline week) to 86.98% (22,790 attempts). The drop is statistically and practically significant. The daily view shows the dip starting on 17 Sep and the lowest day being 18 Sep at 86.66%, against a median of 89.72%.
Kestrel Bank was the segment that concentrated the drop: its success rate fell 11.54pp from 90.03% to 78.49%. The other acquirers (Northstar, Meridian, Saffron) did not change significantly.

Within Kestrel Bank only card payments were hit. Debit card fell 30.11pp (86.42% to 56.31%), credit card fell 28.71pp (88.64% to 59.94%) and card EMI fell 23.87pp (80.67% to 56.80%). UPI, wallet and netbanking at Kestrel showed no significant change.
The failure code ACQ_TIMEOUT (a technical acquirer timeout) rose from 0.26 to 32.27 per 100 attempts on Kestrel's affected card methods (22 to 803 failures). Other failure codes were flat or lower.
Across all acquirers, ACQ_TIMEOUT rose from 0.08 to 3.58 per 100 attempts (815 failures in the current window); no other failure code moved by more than 0.16 per 100 attempts.

The hourly timeline shows the Kestrel card problem running about 36 hours, from 17 Sep 10:00 to 18 Sep 22:00. The worst hour was 18 Sep 02:00, with a 36.36% success rate against a reference of 86.87%. It affected 2,229 attempts and caused about 716 excess failed attempts.
The data-quality scan found no issues (0 findings).

response.headline: The 17 Sep dip was a Kestrel Bank card problem: acquirer timeouts hit Kestrel's debit card, credit card and card EMI payments from 10:00 on 17 Sep, and the overall rate fell 3.10pp from 90.07% to 86.98% across 17-18 Sep.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Ask Kestrel Bank for their incident log and root cause for 17 Sep 10:00 to 18 Sep 22:00, and check our gateway logs for timeout errors on Kestrel's card routes in that window.
hypotheses.rationale: The drop is confined to one acquirer and to its card methods only, with ACQ_TIMEOUT jumping from 0.26 to 32.27 per 100 attempts there. UPI and wallet at the same acquirer were unaffected, which points to a card-specific path rather than a general issue.
hypotheses.text: A Kestrel Bank-side technical incident (for example a connectivity or processing problem on the card authorisation path) caused the timeouts.

recommendations.rationale: The 36-hour Kestrel card degradation accounts for the dip and caused about 716 excess failed attempts.
recommendations.text: Raise an incident with Kestrel Bank and request a root-cause report and confirmation that card processing is back to normal.

recommendations.rationale: The problem ran for about 36 hours before ending, and the signal was very clear: ACQ_TIMEOUT rose from 0.26 to 32.27 per 100 attempts on Kestrel's card methods.
recommendations.text: Set up an alert on ACQ_TIMEOUT per 100 attempts and on hourly success rate by acquirer and payment method, so a similar episode is caught within hours.

recommendations.rationale: Other acquirers held their rates (Northstar -0.44pp, Meridian +0.27pp, Saffron +0.24pp), so rerouting could have limited the impact.
recommendations.text: Evaluate smart routing or failover of card traffic to other acquirers when Kestrel's timeout rate spikes.
